newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican union pledges to back PRI, dissidents boo.
newsitem.headline: Mexican union pledges to back PRI, dissidents boo.

text.p: Leaders of Mexico's second biggest union federation on Tuesday called on members to vote for the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in key elections next month but some dissidents responded with boos and wolf-whistles.

"We are convinced that only the PRI can guarantee the rights of Mexican workers," said Jorge Sanchez, president of the Youth Federation of the Revolutionary Confederation of Workers and Peasants (CROC).

As President Ernesto Zedillo looked on stony-faced from the stage, workers booed and jeered Sanchez when he praised the Zedillo government. Sanchez was forced to cut his speech short because of the heckling, reporters at the event said.
"In this electoral year...we CROC workers, loyal to our revolutionary origin are working for our party to win a legislative majority," Sanchez said.
Zedillo spoke afterwards and was listened to in silence, though applause was polite rather than enthusiastic.
"Tell your comrades that the President of the Republic is the top ally of the Mexican workers," he said.
The 4.5 million-member CROC has backed the PRI since the two organisations were created after the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution.
On July 6, some 52 million registered voters will elect a new lower house of congress, a quarter of the senate, six state governors and the first elected mayor of Mexico City.

Polls show the PRI, which has ruled Mexico for 68 unbroken years, may lose its lower house majority for the first time as opposition parties rise and citizens reel from the 1994-5 economic crisis that gutted their living standards.
